hooks.text: A cosmic structure ten billion light-years long shouldn't exist.
Something spans ten percent of the entire observable universe.
Our models say this 10 billion light-year structure is impossible.

title: The Cosmic Wall That Defies Physics
description: Discover the Hercules-Corona Borealis Great Wall, a structure so large it shouldn't exist according to our models of the universe.

beats.text: A cosmic structure ten billion light-years long shouldn't exist.
beats.visual: Artist concept of a vast galaxy filament superstructure

beats.text: In 2013, astronomers led by Istvan Horvath mapped the locations of massive stellar explosions called gamma-ray bursts.
beats.visual: Artist concept of a gamma-ray burst from a dying massive star

beats.text: Using NASA’s Swift satellite, the team discovered a strange clustering toward the constellation Hercules.
beats.visual: NASA Swift Gamma-Ray Burst Mission spacecraft artist concept

beats.text: These bursts revealed a hidden superstructure spanning roughly ten billion light-years—one-tenth of the entire observable universe.
beats.visual: Large scale structure galaxy wall illustration
queries: all sky map gamma ray bursts

beats.text: It is so immense that it defies our core law that matter is evenly spread through space.
This record-breaker's name was actually coined by a Filipino teenager on Wikipedia, not the discovering scientists.
beats.visual: Wikipedia logo on a white background

beats.text: Critics argue it could be a statistical illusion, leaving the structure's true reality to be proven by future telescopes.
beats.visual: Conceptual design of the proposed THESEUS space telescope mission

beats.text: Our best maps of the early universe suggest that a cosmic structure ten billion light-years long shouldn't exist.
